primary_carrier: Beurling-Nyman criterion (L2[0,1] closure of Muntz fractions)

carrier_definition.atom_definition: rho_a(t) = {a/t} - a {1/t}, where {x} is fractional part
carrier_definition.variant_note: Equivalent formulations use dilations of {1/(a x)} on (0,infty) or restricted countable parameter sets after Bae z-Duarte refinement.

muntz_subspace.name: M_BN
muntz_subspace.definition: closed linear span of rho_a for 0<a<=1 in L2(0,1)
muntz_subspace.finite_windows: M_A = span{rho_a : a in A} for finite A
muntz_subspace.dense_countable_refinement: Bae z-Duarte permits restriction to discrete/countable parameter sets such as integer dilations in the strengthened criterion

parent_residual_on_BN.name: Xi_BN
parent_residual_on_BN.zero_condition: Xi_BN=0 iff one belongs to M_BN

CRE_status_reason: The Beurling-Nyman theorem states Xi_BN=0 iff RH.

CRCFT_mode_classification.reason: The closure condition is target-equivalent to RH.  Gram matrix entries are computable, so the blocker is not missing matrix data but the infinite closure limit.
CRCFT_mode_classification.CTMT_subinterface: finite Gram-matrix projection distances provide a carrier-native matrix interface, but controlling their limit is exactly the target-equivalent Beurling-Nyman criterion
CRCFT_mode_classification.BF_status: not a bridge-failure; the carrier is native and well-defined
